summary: Two things matter today. First, WMT's estimated 11-19 print is now 5 trading days out, inside the window, and no headline or filing confirms the date; meanwhile the PT raises keep coming (BofA $139, Gordon Haskett $130, BTIG $140). Second, a report that Nvidia's board may remove Jensen Huang (NVDA about -8% premarket, CFO Kress floated as interim CEO) arrives 3 trading days before Nvidia's 11-17 earnings. It reversed the 11-11 CoreWeave-led tech rally and pushed BTC below $73K, the same day MSCI confirmed it is removing Strategy from its indexes. Applying L2, I checked every name in the events file against its own estimate and filings. No holding has an 8-K in the 7-day window and none filed a 4.01, 4.02 or 5.02. TTEK reported 11-11 (beat) and SBH's 11-12 estimate is stale.

event_risk.why: Held. The 11-19 date is an estimate (last year's date + 364 days), now 5 trading days out (11-13, 16, 17, 18, 19), so it is inside the high-risk window for any add. No 8-K, results-date headline or company confirmation is in the input, so the date is still unverified, as flagged on 11-10 and 11-11. The PT drift keeps building: BofA to $139 from $126 (11-11), Baird $140, Gordon Haskett to $130 from $110 and a Deutsche Bank adjustment (11-12), and BTIG reiterating Buy at $140 (11-12). That is the seventh or eighth raise in four sessions, so expectations are high going into the print. Per the PM's own L7 note, a close-based stop does not protect against a gap. No filings.

New facts and a dated event. A report says the Nvidia board is weighing Huang's future, with CFO Colette Kress considered for interim CEO, and NVDA traded about -8% premarket with Nasdaq futures lower. Polymarket puts the odds of a higher S&P open at 33%. Nvidia reports on 11-17 (Benzinga: 'Nov. 17 earnings'), 3 trading days out, and the stock is the index's largest AI weight. One opinion piece says NVDA could fall 25% if Huang leaves. This reverses the 11-11 rally (Nasdaq 100 +2.8% and tech up more than $500B after CoreWeave's 25% jump), so the CoreWeave test flagged 11-11 passed for the bulls before today's shock. I raised this back from medium to high because there is now a dated catalyst. Caveat: my QQQ flags since 10-20 graded mostly wrong at 5 days, so weigh this as event risk, not as a direction call.

Fell below $73K this morning on the Nvidia/Huang report ('fresh Black Monday test'). The 11-11 Benzinga piece warned that failing to reclaim $75.7K could expose a break below $73K, and that has now happened. The dated MSCI decision flagged on 11-10 and 11-11 is resolved: MSCI confirmed it will remove Strategy from its benchmark indexes and Strategy fell about 6% premarket. That is negative for crypto-treasury demand. Regulatory overhang continues: O'Leary says institutions need the CLARITY Act, Kalshi faces possible CFTC charges (a prediction market, not a crypto exchange), and Hougan expects volatility under a Democratic Congress. Exchange-failure clause: untripped, since no exchange failed in this input. The Ledger CEO's $8.7B 2026 theft total is context. Bullish items (Adam Back's $1M by 2028, Lavish's $500K, Tim Warren) are opinion. I have no mark, so if a BTC position or stop is live, the PM must compute it.
Moves with BTC. It is only tagged on roundups ('Steady' 11-11, the Schwartz selling item). No ETH-specific event. The Nvidia shock and the MSCI removal apply.

No VOO-specific event. The index's largest weight faces a CEO-ouster report and reports earnings 11-17, inside the window. A Benzinga piece calls NVDA earnings 'earnings day for your 401(k)' because of S&P concentration. Rates backdrop: the 10-year was at 5% after CPI. Retail is buying index ETFs while hedge funds go underweight AI, which is flows, not an event.

Today's tagged item is the Thorne opinion piece warning against a 'reckless' 50bp hike, which adds no new fact. I lowered this from high to medium because there is no new datum and the next dated catalyst (12-09) is outside the 5-day window. The rates risk itself is unchanged.

A second day of M&A chatter (Benzinga 'Watching Clorox Shares; Traders Circulate M&A Chatter', 11-11) follows the 11-10 unconfirmed M&A-blog rumor. There is still no filing or named-outlet report, so it is rumor premium that can reverse. It reported 11-02; next estimate 2027-02-02.

It reported 11-11 after the close (8-K 2.02/8.01/9.01 filed 11-12): Q4 adj EPS $0.49 vs $0.47 and sales $1.340B vs $1.151B est, FY27 GAAP EPS guide $1.65-$1.80 vs $1.71 and sales $4.425B-$4.625B vs $4.497B, Q1 guide in line. Shares were up about 8.5% premarket and Baird raised its PT to $40 (Neutral). This resolves the 11-09 to 11-11 flags, and the file's 11-11 estimate was right. The 8.01 content is not in the input. notable.headline: Nvidia Board Weighs CFO Colette Kress For Interim CEO Role Amid Uncertainty Over Jensen Huang's Future: Report; Stock Market Today: NVDA Stock Sinks Nasdaq, S&P 500 Futures as Board Weighs Jensen Huang's Future
notable.read: This escalates the Huang probe thread that started 11-09. What was a board review is now reported succession planning, and it lands 3 trading days before Nvidia's 11-17 earnings. It came the morning after CoreWeave's beat lifted the Nasdaq 100 2.8%, so the AI trade has whipsawed two days running. It hits the QQQ, VOO and VTI sleeves through concentration.

notable.headline: Bitcoin Dumps Below $73,000 as NVDA Plunges 8% on Huang Ouster Report
notable.read: A third leg down after the break below $75K (11-09) and the post-CPI slide to $73K (11-10). The 11-11 warning that losing $73K was next played out within a day. Crypto is trading as high-beta AI and rates risk. It is not an exchange failure.

notable.headline: Strategy Shares Fall About 6% After MSCI Confirms Index Removal
notable.read: Resolves the dated MSCI crypto-treasury decision flagged 11-10 and 11-11: the removal is confirmed under the new non-operating-company rules. This removes a passive bid from the biggest corporate BTC holder and is a negative for crypto-treasury demand. Tagged MSCI, but it is not MSCI's own risk.

notable.headline: Tech Stocks Add Over $500 Billion as CoreWeave's Blockbuster Results Rescue AI Rally
notable.read: Closes the CoreWeave test flagged 11-09 to 11-11. The result was a margin beat and a lighter funding plan, CRWV +25%, and a rebound in chips, memory and power names. The neocloud demand worry (Microsoft reassessing deals) did not show up in the print.

notable.headline: Analysts Adjust Price Targets on Walmart (Gordon Haskett $130 from $110, Deutsche Bank); BTIG Reiterates Buy, $140; BofA Raises Walmart Price Target to $139
notable.read: This continues the run of pre-print PT raises (UBS, JPMorgan, BMO, Mizuho, Baird earlier). The estimated 11-19 print is now inside the 5-day window and still unconfirmed. The consensus is crowded bullish, which raises the bar for the print.
